In order to strengthen and amplify a national consensus for
peace with progress, USAID assumes Afghan public consent
will be essential for the success of any peace agreement.
The Taliban and other influential state and non-state groups
are effectively using disinformation and hate speech to
undermine and exacerbate peace in Afghanistan. Through
social listening this activity identified, analyzed and
contextualized narrative trends, particularly of disinformation
and hate speech, across social and traditional media.
Informed by these destructive narratives, the activity
proactively supported fact based news and messaging in
support of the Afghan peace process. Additionally,
understanding of these malign narratives contextualized an
intensive three-day workshop with regional Afghan journalists
and government communications officials, enabling forthright
and fact based reporting to improve Afghans' understanding
of, and manage their expectations about, the peace process.
If the Afghan government, civil society, and media increase
accurate and transparent awareness of the peace process
while amplifing Afghans' demand for peace, reconciliation ano
progress, then the influnce of spoilers and beligerents to the
peace process will be reduced, and chance of success for the
Afghan Peace Negotiations will be strengthened.

knowledge, participation, accountability, and inclusion.
Knowledge relates to citizens' understanding of their rights

knowledge, they may be inspired to participate in processes

engagement. If participation is effective and government
actors believe it is constructive, the government may
demonstrate a form of accountability by acknowledging
citizen demands and inviting dialogue about how to improve
policies and services, thereby building trust and partnership
between citizens and government. At this stage policies are
likely to be more responsive to the desires of citizens.

occurs, thereby bringing in more participants, advancing

participants expands; a growing sense emerges that civic

Research Authoritarianism and Disinformation
To understand how distorted information is being used
to gain and maintain unchecked and unaccountable
power in Asia and the Pacific, USAID/Asia Bureau's
Technical Services requested, under the Asia Emerging
Opportunities mechanism, an analysis of how
information disorder affirms authoritarianism and
destabilizes democracy in Asia and the Pacific.
In discussing the scope of work with the USAID/Asia
Bureau, the research team received guidance that
the analysis should present a series of in-depth country
case studies that examine if and, if so, how
information disorder affirms authoritarianism and
destabilizes democracy in Asia and the Pacific. The
team
approached this question through a series of in-depth
country case studies that concentrated on identifying
supply- and demand-side factors that contribute to
information disorder at the national and subnational
levels in four countries in Asia and the Pacific. The case
study countries are the Kyrgyz Republic, Nepal,
Papua New Guinea, and Thailand. The countries
represent regime types ranging from relatively
democratic
political systems to de facto military dictatorships.
